stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{45}{9 - x} \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = 4 \) is \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 9 \left(\frac{x - 4}{5}\right)^{n} \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = -1 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because \( x = -1 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -1 < x < 9 \) excludes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 4\right| < 5 \), the interior \( -1 < x < 9 \), and \( x = -1 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = -1 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 9 (-1)^{n} \), whose terms do not approach 0, so it diverges there. The interval of convergence is \( -1 < x < 9 \).
No, because \( x = -1 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -1 < x < 9 \) excludes.

options.label: Yes, because the geometric sum \( \frac{9}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{9}{2} \) equals \( f(-1) \).
options.derivation: the geometric sum formula applied with ratio -1, whose size is not less than 1

options.label: Yes, because \( x = -1 \) lies in the interval of convergence \( -1 \le x < 9 \).
